title: The $3,000 Card Balance That Takes 15 Years to Clear

beats.say: A $3,000 credit card balance can easily outlast your car, your job, and your phone.
beats.visual: Low angle extreme close-up of a dark worn credit card resting on wet asphalt under a single amber sodium light at night.

beats.say: When you swipe that plastic card, banks don't demand you pay everything back next month.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a hand holding a credit card over a dark counter, cold fluorescent lighting in an empty room, high angle.

beats.say: They only ask for a tiny minimum payment, but where's that money actually going?
beats.visual: Extreme close-up shot of an unbranded paper statement sitting on a dark metal surface, lit by blue hour light.

beats.say: Most people assume paying the required minimum steadily clears away what they borrowed.
beats.visual: Fog cutting across a deserted city street late at night, solitary streetlamp creating dramatic shadows on damp concrete.

beats.say: Here's the reality: at 24% interest, a minimum payment is just 1% plus interest.
beats.visual: Cold fluorescent light illuminating a stark stainless steel table in a dark underpass, low angle view.

beats.say: Because of that, your check doesn't touch the principal. How long until you're finally debt-free?
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a tiny human silhouette walking along an empty highway at night under distant sodium lights.

beats.say: Paying only the minimum on a $3,000 balance takes 183 months. That's over 15 full years.
beats.visual: Rain-slick street at night with soft light reflections, extreme wide view showing an endless row of dark structures.

beats.say: Across those 15 years, you won't just return $3,000. You'll hand over $4,887 in interest alone.
beats.visual: High angle shot of a solitary dark bench in a concrete transit station lit by a single harsh overhead light.

beats.say: So what happens if you raise that monthly check from the minimum up to $300?
beats.visual: Dramatic mountain ridge line silhouette against a deep blue hour sky, cold misty atmospheric view.

beats.say: Paying $300 a month clears that $3,000 balance in 12 months, costing just $381 in interest.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a stark concrete building edge against a dark moody overcast night sky.

beats.say: That single decision cuts 14 years of payments and saves over $4,500 in wasted interest.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of dark moving water reflecting a single distant yellow streetlamp.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you, so your balance doesn't outlast your future.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a tiny silhouette standing on a high ridge looking out over foggy open water at dusk.

caption:
Paying the minimum on a credit card isn't progress—it's profit for the bank. Here is the math on a $3,000 balance.

#moneymath #creditcarddebt #debtfree #personalfinance #quietmoney
description: Learn how credit card minimum payments work and why a $3,000 balance at 24% APR takes over 15 years to pay off when paying only the minimum. Compare the exact cost of minimum payments against paying $300 a month.
first_comment: Have you ever checked how many years your credit card minimum payment will take?

facts.claim: A $3,000 balance at 24% APR paying minimum (1% + interest, min $25) takes 183 months (~15 years) and costs $4,887 in interest.

facts.claim: The same $3,000 balance at 24% APR paid at $300/month takes 12 months and costs $381 in interest.
facts.basis: Money Fact Sheet: Same $3,000 at 24% paying $300/month: 12 months, $381 interest
